diagnosis: Customer on legacy_auth asks about migration steps and rollback options. Per kb-0012, migration involves creating scoped keys, cutting over, then disabling legacy tokens; it is irreversible once legacy tokens are disabled.
reply: Thanks for reaching out! Migrating to Unified Auth replaces your account-wide tokens with scoped keys. The recommended approach is to plan for a dual-running window: first create your scoped keys, then cut traffic over to them, and finally disable the legacy token. Please note that once the legacy tokens are disabled, the migration cannot be reversed, so we suggest completing the cutover and validating everything works before disabling the legacy token. Let us know if you have questions as you plan the migration.
